description: Noisy-channel orthographic recovery of error-full human text: a TYPED edit model (typo kinds cheaper than flat edits) for P(observed|intended) times the grown lexicon + context for P(intended); recovered = Argmax(error_likelihood x context_fit), context breaking the shape-ties (form vs from). The same recogniser loop as the ear, at the letter level.

microtheory.name: error_recovery
microtheory.description: recover intended text from noisy human input

attrs.name: error_recovery
attrs.description: Recover intended text from error-full human input by the NOISY CHANNEL, the SAME loop as acoustic key-recovery but at the ORTHOGRAPHIC level: observed = intended + noise, recover argmax_intended P(intended|observed) proportional to P(observed|intended) x P(intended). A typed word is an intended word pushed through a leaky keyboard, as a heard word is one pushed through a leaky room; reuse ranked() over the GraphLexicon, cochleagram swapped for letter-string. Downstream rules read the recovered token, never the noise.

attrs.name: recovery_error_model
attrs.head: error recovery
attrs.body: P(observed|intended) is a TYPED edit cost over the shape matchers (Levenshtein/DtwTo/BlendCover): a transposition (hiw->how) is one cheap swap not two subs, a doubling/drop (errrs->errors) a cheap run-length edit, a keyboard-adjacent substitution cheap, a phonetic swap (fone->phone) cheap only under the sound-shape matcher; BlendCover segments a run-on back into lexicon words

attrs.name: recovery_prior
attrs.head: error recovery
attrs.body: P(intended) is the GROWN lexicon (a word never met cannot be the answer) times CONTEXT (the surrounding recovered words, the function-word klass, the situation model); candidates are only lexicon words within a small edit radius (1-2), so the whole lexicon is never searched

attrs.name: recovery_decision
attrs.head: error recovery
attrs.body: recovered = Argmax over candidates of (error_likelihood x context_fit); context breaks the ties the error model cannot — form and from are each one transposition apart and equally cheap on shape, so the prior decides by which neighbour the function-word/situation context expects

attrs.name: recovery_test
attrs.head: error recovery
attrs.body: seed a corrupted corpus with known intent and score recovery error-model-only vs error x context; pass = typos recover near-perfectly on SHAPE alone AND the form/from tie-pairs flip CORRECTLY only when context is switched on — that contrast proves the prior does real work, not mere spell-match
